rows.name: New Hampshire
rows.notes: A single statewide final close cannot be established from an official page. RSA 659:4 (and 659:4-a for town ballot questions) sets only a floor: polls open no later than 11 a.m. and close no earlier than 7 p.m., with the city council fixing hours in cities. No statutory latest time exists, and RSA 659:3 lets voters at a polling place vote to close early once everyone on the checklist has voted. Municipal practice varies: Hampton posts 7 am to 8 pm for Nov 3, 2026, Dover posts 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. So 20:00 ET is at least the latest known close, but I could not prove no town closes later. Recommended display: 'Closes no earlier than 7 p.m.; many places close at 8 p.m.; check your town clerk.' The sos.nh.gov pages I opened in the browser pane (At the Polls on Election Day, the 2026-2027 Political Calendar page) do not state polling hours; the Political Calendar PDF the existing data cites returns 403 to curl and I could not read it, so no state-office quote is available. Existing site data (hours set by municipality, close no earlier than 7 p.m.) is consistent with the statute. Election-Day verification (Nov 3, 2026): RSA 659:4 remains a 7:00 p.m. floor with hours set locally; 7:00 p.m. and 8:00 p.m. closes are in effect in different municipalities today (e.g. Milford's official page shows 8:00 p.m.), and the Secretary of State's 2026 pages state no single statewide final closing time. The UNVERIFIED treatment stands: check the local election office.

rows.name: North Dakota
rows.split_zone_note: Poll hours vary by county, opening 7:00-9:00 a.m. and closing 7:00-9:00 p.m. local (ND SOS media guide); times shown are the latest closes. 9:00 p.m. Central / 9:00 p.m. Mountain; all polls closed 11:00 p.m. ET.
rows.notes: Not a single statewide time. NDCC 16.1-01-03: polls open at nine a.m. or earlier (not before seven a.m.) and stay open until seven p.m. or a later hour, not later than nine p.m., as designated per precinct by the city or county governing body. The SOS 2026 General Election media guide says 'Poll Hours are determined by county commissions and vary by county' and points to vote.nd.gov/myvotinginfo for the county list (not opened). Recorded the LATEST permitted close, 21:00 local; the earliest a precinct may close is 19:00. ND spans Central and Mountain time; I list both zones but the sources do not name the Mountain-time counties. Matches existing data (closing 7 to 9 p.m.). Voters in line at closing may vote (ignored). | Central time zone: latest permitted closing time; each precinct closes between 19:00 and 21:00 as set by its city or county governing body (Central time) | Mountain time zone: latest permitted closing time, same 19:00-21:00 window (Mountain-time part of ND); the sources I opened do not list which counties Election-Day verification (Nov 3, 2026): the SOS media guide states poll hours are determined by county commissions and vary; the SOS polling-place lookup lists per-county hours (e.g. Adams County 9:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m.). The closes shown are the latest permitted/designated, not a uniform statewide close.

rows.name: Oregon
rows.split_zone_note: 8:00 p.m. Mountain / 8:00 p.m. Pacific; all polls closed 11:00 p.m. ET
rows.notes: All-mail state: recorded the Election Day ballot-deposit deadline, not a poll close. Ballots mailed with an Election Day postmark may arrive up to 7 days later (ORS 254.470); not part of the deadline recorded. The SOS page also says county elections offices are open 7 a.m. - 8 p.m. on Election Day, and the SOS drop-site list (FINAL 10/30/2026) says 'All drop sites are open until 8 PM Election Day'. Electors in line at 8 p.m. are treated as having begun voting (ORS 254.470(12)), ignored per brief. Malheur County is the Mountain-time area; I put it on America/Boise because the brief asks for one close per zone, but no opened page states the zone. Matches existing data (8 p.m. drop deadline). | Mountain time zone: Malheur County (Mountain time): Malheur County Clerk says drop boxes close 8:00 pm; its page does not name a time zone | Pacific time zone: statewide: last time to return a ballot to a drop box or county elections office on Election Day (all-mail state; there are no polling places)
